title: Removed sticky implementers return after a daemon restart

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: An operator resets an override and restarts the daemon. A resumed run returns to its saved model even though the reset removed that model from its routing cell.

reproduction.output:
C1 before restart claude/sonnet-5.5
C1 after restart codex/luna

codex.evidence: HEAD initializes changedCells as an empty process-local Set. Lines 256–262 discard a removed preference only when that set contains the cell; lines 348 and 365 otherwise append and pin the saved implementer. Reopening the Store after reset reconstructs an unchanged base policy, so startup records no edited cell. Base pinned saved implementers unconditionally and had no operator reset feature.
codex.reason: Reset persistence does not preserve the information needed to reject an obsolete saved implementer after restart.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: The operator overrides a cell so a run's implementer moves to a new model, later resets the override, and the daemon then restarts (for example on a deploy). The resumed run stays pinned to the model the reset removed instead of routing from the restored cell, which the request says must not happen.

reproduction.command: HOME=$TMPDIR/adj/home bun test $TMPDIR/adj/sticky.test.ts  (set implement.medium=[codex/luna], route, reset, reopen Store + new Router/RuntimePolicy, route with prefer)
reproduction.output:
impl under operator codex/luna@medium
in-process after reset claude/sonnet-5.5
after restart codex/luna@medium

opus.evidence: router.ts:256-260 `const edited = this.changedCells.has(`${role}.${complexity}`) || ...; if (edited && !groups.some(...)) preference = undefined;` changedCells is a process-local Set filled only by setPolicy diffs. At startup the Router is built with code+evals and RuntimePolicy calls `router.setPolicy(this.merge(this.operator))`. After a reset this is identical to the base, so no cell is marked changed and `if (c.prefer && preference) consider([c.prefer])` appends the removed implementer and pins it first.
opus.reason: Removing a sticky implementer depends on in-memory edit tracking that is lost on restart, so a removal done by a reset comes undone.

title: Historical edits permanently disable stickiness for escalated implementers

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: A run escalates to a stronger model after an operator edit. Its next round drops that model and returns to the weaker routing-cell model, undoing the escalation.

reproduction.output: C2 escalation claude/opus next round codex/sol

codex.evidence: HEAD setPolicy only adds entries to changedCells; it never clears them or distinguishes selections made before and after an edit. The condition 'if (edited && !groups.some(...)) preference = undefined' therefore rejects a subsequently escalated implementer too. Base retained the preferred implementer without this condition.
codex.reason: This is the historical-edit invalidation mechanism identified by G1.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: After any operator edit to the implement cell, a run that escalates to a stronger model outside that cell loses it on the next round and falls back to the weaker cell model. The escalation is undone for the rest of the daemon's life.

reproduction.command: HOME=$TMPDIR/adj/home bun test $TMPDIR/adj/sticky.test.ts  (edit implement.medium, escalate with minTier 5, route next round with prefer=escalated)
reproduction.output:
escalated claude/opus
next round codex/luna@medium
no-edit router, same prefer claude/opus

opus.evidence: router.ts:49 `private readonly changedCells = new Set<string>()`. Entries are added in setPolicy and never removed, so `edited` stays true forever, and any preference outside the current groups is dropped even when it was chosen after the edit.

title: Detect signals executed inside shell expansions

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: An agent sends a signal inside a shell substitution in a double-quoted argument or an unquoted heredoc. Neither harness produces the required warning, so the attempt is absent from the warning feed and report count.
codex.evidence: HEAD tokenizes an entire double-quoted argument as one token and subsequently skips it after recognizing echo. For heredocs, it scans the body only when SH.test(base) or JS.test(base) succeeds, then replaces the entire body with `${rest}\n`. Shell command substitutions execute in both double-quoted arguments and unquoted heredocs regardless of the receiving command. The throwaway script passed command strings through the detector and both production harness parsers; it did not execute any signal commands. signals.ts does not exist at base.
codex.reason: The new detector discards executable shell substitutions as literal argument or heredoc contents.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: An agent runs a kill command hidden inside a double-quoted command substitution, such as echo "$(kill -TERM 123)", or inside a heredoc fed to cat. The shell still runs the kill, but no warning reaches the event log, the feed or the report.

reproduction.command: bun -e 'import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; for (const c of ["echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\"", "cat <<EOF\n$(kill 123)\nEOF", "echo $(kill 123)"]) console.log(JSON.stringify(c), signalCommand(c));'
reproduction.output:
"echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\"" false
"cat <<EOF\n$(kill 123)\nEOF" false
"echo $(kill 123)" true

opus.evidence: signals.ts:28 tokenizes a whole double-quoted string as one token (`"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"`). That token is only matched as a command name and is never scanned again for $(...). signals.ts:19-25 replaces the body of any heredoc whose command is not sh or node/bun with nothing ('anything else (cat > file) is literal data'), but an unquoted heredoc still expands $(...). An unquoted substitution is detected only because the tokenizer splits on '('. The file calls itself 'Advisory recognition of ordinary executable forms', and these forms are unusual for an agent that is just reaching for pkill or kill.
opus.reason: Reproduced: a kill that runs inside a double-quoted substitution or an unquoted heredoc is not detected, but this only affects the advisory detector and needs unusual command forms.

title: Provide writable isolated state for the confined Codex CLI

codex.criterion: stops the factory or the running release from working
codex.failure_scenario: A factory run starts a normal Codex agent using the operator's usual state directory. The new outer sandbox denies required runtime state writes, so the agent cannot initialize and Codex-backed runs stop before doing their work.

codex.evidence: HEAD adds runSandboxed around every tool-enabled Codex invocation. Its roots permit writes only to scratch and, for editors, the checkout. seatbeltProfile declares `(deny file-write*)` before granting those roots. However, the invocation still uses `env: agentEnv(scratchEnv(spec))`; scratchEnv overrides only TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP, preserving HOME/CODEX_HOME. buildCodexArgs adds --ephemeral only for privateSession. Base launched the same persistent CLI directly without this outer write restriction. The offline permission probe independently reproduced the initialization failure without network access. Full production Seatbelt integration is unreproduced because this worker rejects even a permissive nested sandbox. This is a runtime-state write failure, distinct from G1's nested-sandbox initialization failure.
codex.reason: The new whole-process write restriction makes ordinary Codex runtime state unwritable without providing an isolated writable replacement.

codex.failure_scenario: An unrelated background task starts in the same directory while an agent command runs. Finishing the agent command kills that unrelated task, crossing the invocation's process ownership boundary.

reproduction.output: {"claim":"C1","invocationExit":0,"unrelatedPid":16902,"unrelatedAlive":false}

codex.evidence: HEAD accepts an unmarked orphan when `parents.get(pid) === 1`, its birth time is after invocation start, and `path === directory || path.startsWith(...)`. No ancestry or invocation marker is required. The reproduction launched the empty-environment, detached sleep through an independent launcher. HEAD killed it; running the same probe against base preserved it (`unrelatedAlive:true`). Base signals only the invocation's process group.
codex.reason: Directory and birth time select processes that the invocation does not own.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: While an invocation is running in a worktree, some unrelated process with no visible environment, whose parent has already exited, starts in that worktree or the scratch directory. When the invocation ends, Limitless treats it as its own and kills it.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/c1.ts $PWD  (runProcess runs `sleep 1.5` in a temp dir; meanwhile the outer test process, not the invocation, starts `/bin/sh -c '/bin/sleep 30 &'` with env={}, detached, in the same dir, so the sleep is orphaned)
reproduction.output: {"unrelatedPid":21811,"unrelatedAlive":false}

opus.evidence: processes-darwin.ts:52-70: `if (parents.get(pid) !== 1) return false; const born = readBorn(); ... if (born < started) return false; const cwd = readCwd(); ... return directories.some((directory) => path === directory || path.startsWith(...))`. Line 189 `if (offset === length) hidden.add(pid);` and line 227 `for (const pid of hidden) if (parents.get(pid) === 1 && isMember(pid)) marked.add(pid);`. Ownership comes only from being an orphan with an empty environment, born after the invocation started, with a cwd under its roots. Nothing ties the process to this invocation. Base had no such fallback; it only killed its own process group.
opus.reason: Reproduced: the cwd-plus-birth-time orphan fallback killed a process the invocation did not start, but it only applies to orphans with no visible environment, which is a narrow case.

title: Shutdown is confirmed while detached descendants remain alive

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a detached background writer with a fresh environment and a working directory outside the checkout. The invocation reports successful shutdown while the writer continues modifying checkout files through absolute paths, leaving cleanup exposed to the original race.

reproduction.output:
{"claim":"C2","replacementEnvironment":"empty","invocationExit":0,"descendantPid":16924,"descendantAlive":true,"writingAfterReturn":true}
{"claim":"C2","replacementEnvironment":"nonempty","invocationExit":0,"descendantPid":17005,"descendantAlive":true,"writingAfterReturn":true}

codex.evidence: HEAD discovers unmarked processes through current session/group membership, a current parent chain, or the hidden-environment directory fallback. After detachment and parent exit, the writer matches none: lines 228–231 require a recognized ancestor or `hidden.has(pid) && isMember(pid)`, and the fallback rejects its outside directory. Shutdown then returns at proc.ts:203 after two empty discovery snapshots. Both writers also survived at base, so this is an unmet explicit whole-process-tree requirement rather than an introduced Darwin regression.
codex.reason: Successful shutdown does not establish that all invocation descendants have stopped.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle
opus.failure_scenario: A command run by the agent starts a helper in its own session with a replaced environment, then exits. On macOS the shutdown never finds the helper, reports the invocation stopped, and the helper keeps running and can still write into the worktree during cleanup.

reproduction.command: bun $TMPDIR/adj/c2.ts $PWD  (inside runProcess, a bun -e script spawns /bin/sleep 30 with env={FOO:'1'}, cwd='/', detached:true, then exits)
reproduction.output: {"exit":0,"descendantPid":21935,"descendantAlive":true}

opus.evidence: processes-darwin.ts:178-190: a process is a member only if it carries the marker token, matches the leader's session/group, or (via line 230 darwinDescendant) has a marked live ancestor. A setsid child with a replaced environment whose parent already exited (ppid 1) matches none of these. The empty-environment cwd fallback doesn't apply either. stopMarkedProcesses (proc.ts:199-203) then returns once nothing is claimed. The code admits this at processes-darwin.ts:48-50 ('Residuals: a detached platform tool that leaves the worktree...'). Base's process-group kill missed setsid children too, but the request requires the whole process tree to be killed.
opus.reason: Reproduced: a detached descendant with a replaced environment outlives a shutdown reported as confirmed, which falls short of the request's 'background children must not outlive the invocation'.

codex.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
codex.failure_scenario: After a stuck implementer, gate checks time out and trigger a rerun. A one-time cleanup failure before that rerun terminates the run instead of retrying cleanup or advancing to another implement round.

reproduction.output: {"claim":"C3","resolved":false,"errorType":"CommandError","error":"injected one-time cleanup failure","gateTimeoutReruns":1,"cleanCalls":2,"commands":["rev-parse --git-path index","reset --hard -q HEAD","clean -ffdxq","rev-parse --git-path index","reset --hard -q HEAD","clean -ffdxq","status --porcelain"]}

codex.evidence: The isolated reproduction executed HEAD's gates block and actual checkoutCommitted/worktreeGit functions, mocking command execution and gate results without Git writes. The initial cleanup succeeded; the rerun cleanup failed once and was never retried. HEAD passes retryClean at line 1091 but calls `await checkoutCommitted(cwd)` at line 1109, retaining the default false. A successful finally block preserves the resulting CommandError, and line 1164 rethrows anything other than WorktreeCleanError. Base also lacked recovery here; the explicit cleanup-recovery requirement remains incomplete.

opus.criterion: needs an unusual input the request doesn't ask to handle

opus.reproduction: unreproduced: needs a gate-timeout re-run combined with a transient git clean failure. Judged from the quoted code.
opus.evidence: engine.ts:1091 `await checkoutCommitted(cwd, undefined, Boolean(ctx.state.implementerIssue));` but engine.ts:1109 `await checkoutCommitted(cwd);` (retryClean defaults to false, repos.ts:471). A CommandError from it passes through the finally block. The catch at engine.ts:1162-1164 rethrows anything that isn't a WorktreeCleanError, so the run fails. By this point the gate processes have been confirmed stopped, so a transient clean failure here is unlikely.
opus.reason: The second clean before the gate re-run skips the retry and round-failure handling the change added for the first clean, but reaching it needs an unusual combination of events.

title: Shutdown is confirmed while detached descendants remain alive

codex.criterion: a check the change claims to add can be bypassed
codex.failure_scenario: On Linux, an implementer launches a background helper with a replacement environment while keeping it in the invocation's process group. When the invocation ends, cleanup overlooks the helper and it can continue writing during subsequent rounds.
codex.reproduction: unreproduced: this host is Darwin, so the native Linux backend could not be exercised.
codex.evidence: This additional mechanism comes from C2's third variant. HEAD's Linux discovery filters candidates using `carriesMarker((row[4] ?? "").split(/\s+/))` and immediately returns `[]` when none match. It does not use process-group membership as a fallback; shutdown signals only discovered, claimed PIDs. Base's `killTree` used `process.kill(-child.pid, sig)`, including SIGKILL on close, which covered same-group helpers regardless of environment.

opus.criterion: a realistic input in normal operation gives a wrong result or a silent failure
opus.failure_scenario: On Linux, the agent's test suite starts a helper (say a test server) with its own environment instead of the inherited one. When the invocation ends, the helper is no longer killed, although the previous release killed it through the process group, so it keeps writing into the worktree while cleanup and the next round run.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: the host is macOS. The Linux code path (ps eww plus /proc environ) can't run here, so this rests on quoted code.
opus.evidence: Head proc.ts:105-110: `const candidates = environments.filter((row) => ... carriesMarker((row[4] ?? "").split(/\s+/)))` and lines 136-140 check only /proc/<pid>/environ for the marker. There is no group, session or parent-chain check on Linux. stopMarkedProcesses signals only claimed pids (proc.ts:209-217). Base proc.ts:111-114 killed the whole group with `process.kill(-child.pid, sig)`, which caught same-group children whatever their environment. Head has no negative-pid kill (grep finds only `process.kill(pid, signal)` and `child.kill("SIGKILL")`).
opus.reason: Dropping the process-group kill means that on Linux a same-group child that replaces its environment is no longer stopped, which is a regression from base.

title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands

codex.failure_scenario: A verifier ran a command producing periodic output for 30 seconds and received its complete result successfully.

reproduction.output: Bun 1.4.3: MCP response received after 30263ms; subprocess durationMs=30260, exitCode=0, cancelled=false, timedOut=false, idleTimedOut=false, isError=false.

codex.evidence: The temporary probe exercised HEAD's withReaderCommands and the real MCP client/server transport. Its injected launcher removed Seatbelt wrapping while retaining the actual subprocess and cancellation wiring; temporary scratch creation was redirected under TMPDIR. Both 15-second and 30-second commands succeeded. Although lines 167–169 omit idleTimeout and line 214 enables JSON responses, the claimed ten-second disconnect did not occur. The observed abort notification happened after subprocess completion during MCP cleanup. Base has no reader bridge. This reproduction covers installed Bun 1.4.3, not CI's pinned 1.4.0.
codex.reason: The actual bridge successfully returned commands exceeding the alleged timeout, so the claimed failure is not supported on the available runtime.

opus.failure_scenario: Claimed: a verification command that runs longer than 10 seconds loses its connection to the reader bridge and is killed. On the Bun version this repo uses, Bun does not close a connection while a request is still waiting for its response.

reproduction.command: bun (1.4.3, CI pins 1.4.0) script: Bun.serve({hostname:'127.0.0.1',port:0, fetch: async req => { req.signal.addEventListener('abort',log); await Bun.sleep(25000); return new Response('done') }}) with no idleTimeout set, then curl -X POST to it (also tested with fetch at 13s)
reproduction.output:
done
200 25.004778   (fetch variant: 'client got 200 done', 'aborted false'). No disconnect and no abort of the request signal.

opus.evidence: src/harness/reader.ts:167 `Bun.serve({ hostname: "127.0.0.1", port: 0, async fetch(req) {...} })` sets no idleTimeout. Bun's types say the default is 10, but in practice that idle timer does not fire while the handler is still awaiting. A request that waited 25 seconds with nothing sent finished with 200, and req.signal never aborted. So the abort chain through `AbortSignal.any([... req.signal ...])` is never triggered by the server's idle timeout.
opus.reason: In an empirical test, Bun 1.4.x kept a pending request open for 25 seconds with no idle disconnect, so the claimed mechanism does not occur.

opus.criterion: the previous release breaks on rollback or a newer CLI breaks against an older daemon
opus.failure_scenario: A newer MCP client connects to the previous daemon release and asks list_runs for one repository's runs. The old daemon ignores the repository filter and returns the newest runs from every repository. The agent receives other repositories' runs as matches, and the 'more remain' flag is wrong.
opus.reproduction: unreproduced: I did not rerun the reviewer's probe. The base and head code shown below make the mechanism plain.
opus.evidence: At head, httpBackend.list (mcp.ts:233-236) only adds `...(repo ? { repo } : {})` to the query string. The tool handler then returns `runs.slice(0, limit)` and `hasMore: runs.length > limit` without checking that each run's repoSlug equals the requested repo. The base daemon's /api/runs GET handler (base src/server/http.ts) reads only status, ids and limit, and the `repo` parameter is added only at head (http.ts:405), so an older daemon silently ignores it.
opus.reason: This is the same mechanism as G1: the proxy trusts the daemon to apply the new repo filter, and an older daemon does not.
